Finally saw it yesterday -- and it's utterly phenomenal. I am fairly certain its my favorite Marvel Cinematic Universe movie to date -- I suspect another viewing or two will confirm that. I've been listening to the soundtrack non-stop all morning. Just a fun, fun summer movie that delivered on all levels. It's also a movie that I do not think would have been possible if the preceding 11 films and TV series had not already been made, since so much of the fun of the movie comes from how wonderfully it ties together elements of the MCU's past to the present, and hopefully future.

It also left me with a real desire to see a prequel film featuring Hank Pym's adventures as Ant-Man working for S.H.I.E.L.D. alongside a young Nick Fury, a seasoned Dum Dum Dugan and Peggy Carter, Howard Stark, Alexander Pierce, Thunderbolt Ross, Janet Van Dyne, and more.

My only gripe with the movie is frivolous -- but I wish the Yellowjacket suit buyers had been someone other than Hydra. Something like The Hand, or even a resurgent A.I.M. Something that could have been a neat Easter Egg going forward. In fact the more I think about it, I am really surprised they didn't do just that. It just feels like after Hydra rose and fell in the span of a year that Marvel was done with them, but maybe not quite yet. Grant Ward and all.

Definitely the best cameo in any of these movies to date with Falcon's appearance. More like a full out supporting role. The people in the theater really dug that one. Which is one last awesome anecdote -- the MCU has managed to suck everyone, even the average movie viewer, into their story like some great lasting TV drama. To see "common" Sunday afternoon audiences following along so well and applauding every little reference to something past (as opposed to just the hardcore fans) is pretty impressive. Just another testament to the quality of the work Marvel Studios has put in.

So yeah, TLDR; Ant-Man was amazing, and reports of Marvel's demise have been greatly exaggerated.

Whether or not I should do a full OS encryption with something like Verucrypt.

tl;dr Encrypt your drive, but understand how

So, here's the deal with disk encryption. It's kind of like sex. Doing it half-way may give you some feeling of satisfaction, but it's not really that great if you don't go all in.

To understand why, you need to understand how disk encryption is attacked. The encryption itself isn't attacked, rather it's the fact that the encryption key needs to be stored in memory somewhere. If an attacker can pull the key from memory, your encryption is useless. So what do you do?

First- make sure you do full disk encryption, to include the boot partition. Can't boot? Can't get the encryption key. Unless your computer has a firewire port. Firewire allows Direct Memory Access (DMA), which means an attacker can get to the in-memory encryption key. If your computer has one, I'd consider disabling it. With epoxy.

Understand, though, that even this doesn't offer completely bulletproof protection. Your RAM chips will keep that key in state for awhile (I don't know how long) when the computer has been powered off. If an attacker can get to the RAM and flash-freeze it, then the key can be extracted later.

Most important step of all really:

Do not grant your regular login administrative rights.

Create a second account for administrative tasks, and don't log into it unless you're planning on making a bunch of changes at once. Log in to your regular account, and when installing something or updating or whatever, it will prompt you to provide administrative credentials and you'll do that.

This is a bit of a hassle, but it's the most secure way to set up your computer. The way almost any hack attempt into your PC happens is by latching onto your administrative credentials when you're logged in as an admin.
This is really important for Windows users to understand and practice. Unfortunately it's not well known at all.
